objective: Propose a HYPERBOLIC quality metric for an exported Stage-2 Semantic-ID table that correlates with the Stage-3 test Recall@10 of the run that read it. The metric is a NUMBER computed from the SID table; nothing is trained, no Stage 2 and no Stage 3 run is made, and the metric must be computable in under a minute on 24587 items. It must be judged on 97 SID+recall pairs that already exist.
contract:
A METRIC is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. HYPERBOLIC CONSTRUCTION: the number uses an explicit curved operation -- a Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, a geodesic or Frechet barycentre in a ball of fixed negative curvature, a tangent-space comparison that is only meaningful because of the map. A Euclidean distance in disguise does not qualify, and the proposal must say where the curvature enters.
  2. COMPUTABLE FROM THE TABLE: the inputs are the exported SID table (the integer code per item and level), optionally the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (source/target representations per item, learned on training pairs only) and optionally the TRAINING split. Nothing else.
  3. NO LEAKAGE: no validation interaction and no test interaction may enter the number, directly or through a fitted quantity. A metric that reads the recall, the Stage 3 run, or a validation/test pair is out of scope.
  4. FIXED FORM: no free parameter tuned against the 97 recalls. Any constant must be derived (from the codebook size, the item count, the reference's own temperature) and stated.
  5. ONE NUMBER: the metric returns one scalar per SID table, higher meaning better. Diagnostics that need a second number to interpret are out of scope.
A metric that simply re-expresses the prefix count, the collision rate or the same-bucket ratio is out of scope: those are already measured and the bucket count does not track recall (Spearman -0.065 on the 97 pairs).

metrics.title: Normalized geodesic covering radius of level-1 SID cells about their Poincare Frechet barycentres
metrics.formula:
Let N items, level-1 code c_i in {0..K1-1}, and z_i the frozen reference TARGET representation of item i (in R^d).
  (1) Curve scale: tau = the Issue #126 reference's own temperature if recorded, else tau = 0.5*sqrt(mean_i ||z_i||^2) taken over the TRAINING split only. No recall is read.
  (2) Exp map into the unit Poincare ball (curvature K = -1): x_i = tanh(||z_i|| / (2*tau)) * z_i/||z_i||, and x_i = 0 if z_i = 0. Hence ||x_i|| < 1.
  (3) Hyperbolic distance: dH(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2)) ).
  (4) Mobius ops with lambda_x = 2/(1-||x||^2):
      x (+) y = [ (1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y ] / ( 1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2 )
      exp_x(v) = x (+) tanh(lambda_x * ||v|| / 2) * v/||v||
      log_x(y) = (2/lambda_x) * artanh( lambda_x * ||(-x)(+)y|| ) * ((-x)(+)y) / ||(-x)(+)y||
  (5) For each code b with item set S_b, n_b = |S_b|:
      mu_b^(0) = Euclidean mean of {x_i : i in S_b}; if its norm >= 0.99, rescale it to norm 0.99.
      For t = 0..9 (T = 10, fixed, not tuned):
        mu_b^(t+1) = exp_{mu_b^(t)} ( (1/n_b) * sum_{i in S_b} log_{mu_b^(t)}(x_i) )
      mu_b = mu_b^(10);  r_b = max_{i in S_b} dH(mu_b, x_i),  with r_b = 0 when n_b = 1.
  (6) Whole cloud: mu_all by the same recursion over all N items; R = max_i dH(mu_all, x_i).
  (7) METRIC: M = 1 - sum_{b=1..K1} (n_b / N) * (r_b / R).
  M lies in [0,1], higher is better, one scalar, deterministic, nothing fitted.
metrics.geometry: Fixed negative curvature K = -1 on the unit Poincare ball. Curvature enters at three points none of which can be removed: (a) the exp map at the origin with scale tau places z_i at hyperbolic radius 2*artanh(||x_i||), so equal Euclidean steps near the boundary cost far more than near the centre; (b) every radius is a Poincare geodesic length dH, not a chord; (c) each cell centre is a Frechet (Karcher) barycentre obtained by Riemannian gradient descent in the ball through exp/log maps, which has no closed Euclidean form. A Euclidean mean-and-radius substitute is a different number: it would treat a cell hugging the origin and a cell hugging the boundary as equally tight, which dH deliberately does not.
metrics.why: Prefix retrieval returns the items sharing the level-1 prefix and re-ranks them, so Recall@10 is governed by whether a cell is uniformly tight about its own centre: a single straggler inside a cell can never be retrieved however strong the re-ranker is, yet a mean or a variance-explained score is dominated by the bulk and blind to exactly that item. The covering radius is the quantity the top-10 cut actually sees. Weighting by n_b/N makes the number an item-level statement, "the typical item's worst-case geodesic distance to its cell centre, relative to the whole cloud", so it cannot be gamed by many near-empty cells and so that the max is not carried by a single tiny code. Dividing by R removes the reference's overall spread and temperature, which is what makes tables from different Stage-2 configurations comparable at all. Over Q_H it adds: Q_H is an averaged prefix-ranking score that is unnormalised and collapses at level 2 because the prefix becomes nearly an item id (+0.634 at level 1, +0.287 at level 2); this metric is a worst-case, scale-free, geometry-only statement that stays at level 1 and never touches the level-2 degeneracy that also destroyed the path likelihood.
metrics.compute: N = 24587, K1 = 256, d at most 256. Barycentres need T*N exp/log pairs and about 2*T*N*d flops in total, plus one max per cell; with T = 10 that is ~1.3e8 elementary operations, i.e. well under a second in numpy and a few seconds in pure Python. Memory is O(N*d) for the ball points plus O(N) for the codes. No item-item matrix is ever formed, so the 24587^2 trap is avoided.
metrics.risks:
(1) Degenerate when all level-1 codes coincide: then R = r_b and M = 0, which is the genuinely worst table, so the value stays informative rather than wrong.
  (2) R is a max, so one far-out reference vector inflates R and pushes every table's M toward 1, compressing the cross-run spread. The remedy is to fix R from the TRAINING split a priori, not to choose it by looking at the 97 recalls.
  (3) A strongly anisotropic reference makes all cells look tight and saturates M near 1 for every table, giving near-zero variance and no correlation.
  (4) If level 1 is uninformative and the semantic content lives only in level 2, the metric reads the wrong partition.
  (5) The construction assumes one frozen reference shared by every run; if runs used different reference feature spaces the ball geometries are not comparable and the metric must not be used across them.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on the SID table whose level-1 codes are assigned by radius or norm stratification, for example hashing on the reference norm or a coarse k-means run on ||z_i|| alone. Such a table has a perfectly healthy bucket count (about 96 items per code) and a healthy same-bucket ratio, but each cell is a thin radial shell spanning many angular sectors, so its geodesic covering radius is close to R and M is near 0 while recall is poor, because direction rather than norm carries the neighbourhood. The mirror failure is the fully collapsed table, one code for all 24587 items, which also gives M = 0. These are precisely the two tables on which count-based and likelihood-based metrics are fooled, which is the point of the construction.
